summary: Reviewed all 161 files across the iOS SwiftUI app, React/Vite SPA, and legacy static tree per file-inventory.json, focusing on the largest/flagged files (NetworkService.swift, AccountView.swift, NotesListView.swift, AppState.swift), every hooks-layer file, the full legacy js/ tree, both config.js/utils.js pairs, and codebase-wide greps for empty catches, dead code, and debug logging. Headline findings: (Critical) three incompatible error-handling conventions coexist for the same fetch-call operation class, most severely in useSessions.js and useAgentChat.js where ~23 bare `catch {}` blocks swallow every network failure with zero logging or user feedback, unlike sibling hooks useMessaging.js/useNotes.js which consistently surface failures; the legacy notes.js/messaging.js repeat the same silent-swallow pattern on a surface with no test backstop. (High) verse-parsing logic (not just markup) is copy-pasted verbatim between frontend/js/bible.js and frontend/src/utils.js; two identically-named escHtml functions differ in actual escaping coverage; NetworkService.swift (1453 loc) is a well-documented but monolithic single-file type spanning ~10 unrelated domains. (Medium) AccountView.swift/NotesListView.swift are oversized single-file views with no section-level file split; NetworkService.swift applies its own decode-failure-tagging hardening inconsistently (fetchBookmarks missed vs. its siblings); useSessions.js's ref-mirroring convention for async callbacks isn't shared by sibling hooks. (Low) leftover debug console.log calls in legacy notes.js; NotesPanel.jsx bundles 5 components with duplicated inline hover-style handlers. No TODO/dead-code markers found; documentation quality and naming clarity were generally strong and are called out as not flagged.
